Preliminary results1 suggest that injec- tion of botulinum A toxin into the detrusor muscle can increase functional bladder capacity and restore continence in patients with urinary incontinence (p.2180) after spinal cord injury who are resistant to antimuscarinics. Similar results2 have been found in children with detrusor hyperreflexia caused by myelomenin- gocele. Botulinum A toxin has also been tried in other bladder dysfunc- tions.3,4 Reviews5,6 have concluded that although there is some evidence that injection of botulinum toxins into the detrusor wall can improve symptoms of overactive bladder syndrome, further studies are warranted. In a few small studies7,8 the injection of botulinum A toxin into the prostate gland has been reported to relieve the symptoms of urinary retention associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (p.2178). 1.
